analysis: Integration pass over a Flint serving-speedup PR. Changes: (a) changelog and docs/architecture/inference.md (head ~2336-2347), documentation only. (b) EngineV2KVBackendPolicy.swift:37-41 adds the exact ID "RecursiveSI/flint-int4" to the auto-paged allowlist. Matching is exact-string, and the kill switch, VLM veto and crash-loop guard are unchanged. The test at EngineV2KVBackendPolicyTests confirms prefix cache stays off by default for this ID, so there is no new at-rest surface under T-041. (c) FlintNativeProtocolConstraint.swift:148-162 adds maskCacheKey, which returns the interned state id only when not exhausted, remainingTokens>0 and the state is known. State ids are never reused. The allowed set depends on the budget only through remainingTokens>0, which the guard enforces, so the key maps to one mask. Exhausted or unknown states return nil, preserving the fail-closed empty mask. allowsChainedDecode=true is justified in the comment because nextState interns only host-confirmed tokens. (d) FlintAnswerStopConstraint.swift:70-91 maps matched nodes to key -1 and scanning nodes to the base key, which is always >=0 (checked by `key >= 0`), so there is no collision. Locking is correct: the node is read under the lock, which is then released before calling base. (e) Tests add keys-follow-masks checks, including the nil cases for exhaustion and zero budget. (f) The libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule pointer moves f77b384 to fbd2cd0 with no visible diff. It contains the chained-decode sampler, the device mask cache and the redraw logic, which cannot be verified. The open questions are whether the device mask cache is scoped per request or per constraint instance (state ids are per-instance, so a cache shared across constraints could collide), whether speculative sampling can emit or commit a token sampled with a stale mask, and whether retained logits are released on cancel and retire (T-028, T-010). The width of 8 for flint-int4 depends on existing memory admission (T-029). No concrete regression is established from the visible code. The submodule review is the remaining security-relevant uncertainty.
